ORIGIN.quote: “OpenAI” appears often, yet can be typed by anyone. Therefore attribution to OpenAI or any particular model/operator is only **Medium-to-Low confidence**. The behavioral automation finding does not depend on it.
ORIGIN.reason: A reader clearly learns that OpenAI is the name the evidence points at — the report counts 2,678 OpenAI-bearing labels, cites pages like `OpenAINov05ConstructionLive`, and devotes an attribution section to whether the swarm can be traced to OpenAI — but the report's own verdict is that the strings are “presentation, not authenticated provenance” and can be typed by anyone, so it declines to attribute and notes its findings do not depend on the question. This sits above the pure set-aside band because it grants the hypothesis “Medium-to-Low confidence” rather than dismissing it outright, yet below 0.6 because OpenAI is never left standing as a live leading possibility — it is folded into a generic “any particular model/operator” and downweighted.
